headline: Strict Ferry and Wilderness Camping Quotas
reservation: Access requires a ferry reservation through the official concessionaire, which can book up weeks in advance. Camping permits are managed by the National Park Service and are strictly limited by site capacity; distinguish between Sea Camp and primitive wilderness sites. Always check the official NPS site for current ferry schedules and permit availability.

days.title: Gilded Age Ruins and Wild Horses
days.start: Suggested: 9 AM from St. Marys Ferry Dock

stops.name: Dungeness Mansion Ruins
stops.detail: Walk the skeletal remains of the Carnegie estate where feral horses often graze on the historic lawns.

stops.name: Greene-Miller Cemetery
stops.detail: Visit the final resting place of Revolutionary War figures and island residents amidst the live oaks.

days.driving: Walking or cycling only; no public vehicle access
days.note: The ferry is the only public transport; do not miss the final departure time.

days.title: Maritime Forest and Wilderness Shores

stops.name: Parallel Trail
stops.detail: Hike under a dense canopy of ancient live oaks and saw palmettos to experience the interior ecosystem.

stops.name: Cumberland Island Beach
stops.detail: Explore miles of undeveloped Atlantic coastline for shell collecting and birdwatching.

days.driving: Walking or cycling only; conditions vary with sand depth
days.note: Bring all water and food as no concessions exist on the island.

days.title: North End History
days.start: Suggested: 9 AM via your own bicycle, with ferry bike space arranged in advance

stops.name: Plum Orchard Mansion
stops.detail: Tour a fully preserved Gilded Age manor (check tour times at the dock) located mid-island.

stops.name: First African Baptist Church
stops.detail: Visit The Settlement at the north end, a site of significant post-Civil War African American history.

days.driving: Walking or cycling only; allow 4-6 hours for a round trip to the north end
days.note: The 14-mile round trip to Plum Orchard is strenuous on sandy roads; pace accordingly.

intel.title: Mainland Gateway Parking
intel.text: Complimentary parking is provided near the St. Marys Visitor Center for ferry passengers. Overnight campers must use designated long-term zones.

intel.title: Island-Wide Connectivity Gap
intel.text: Cellular service is unreliable and often non-existent once you leave the Dungeness area. Carry a physical map provided by the National Park Service.

intel.title: Self-Sufficiency Requirement
intel.text: There are no fuel stations, grocery stores, or restaurants on the island. You must pack all necessary supplies from the mainland town of St. Marys.

intel.title: Ferry Departure Deadlines
intel.text: The ferry operates on a strict seasonal schedule; late arrivals will be stranded on the mainland or island. Arrive 30 minutes before your booked departure.

intel.title: Wilderness Permit Boundaries
intel.text: Access to the northern wilderness areas for camping requires specific permits distinct from the ferry ticket. Travel wilderness trails on foot; bicycles are prohibited on trails and may be ridden only where permitted on roads and the designated beach segment.

plan.arrival: Fly to JAX, drive one hour north to St. Marys, and check in at the NPS Visitor Center before boarding the scheduled ferry.
plan.vehicle: Private vehicles are prohibited on the island; mainland parking is for standard vehicles only.
plan.goldenHour: Dungeness Dock provides a viewpoint for the salt marshes at sunset, though evening visitors must be overnight permit holders.
